profile.name: Tanja Liedtke Foundation
profile.tagline: Fostering international contemporary dance theatre connections.
profile.insight: Established in July 2008 following choreographer Tanja Liedtke's death in Sydney, the foundation connects Australian and European contemporary dance.
profile.profile: The Tanja Liedtke Foundation is a German-based charitable organization established in July 2008 in honor of dancer and choreographer Tanja Liedtke. Liedtke died in a car accident in Sydney, Australia, in August 2007, just two months after beginning her tenure as artistic director of the Sydney Dance Company. Registered in Stuttgart, Germany, as a tax-privileged organization (Tanja Liedtke Stiftung), the charity supports contemporary dance theatre and fosters Australian and European artistic exchanges. Its initiatives include international fellowships and production awards in partnership with institutions across Germany and Australia.
profile.profile_long:
ORIGINS AND HISTORY
The Tanja Liedtke Foundation was established in July 2008 to preserve and extend the artistic vision of Tanja Liedtke, a celebrated dancer and choreographer. In June 2007, Liedtke had been appointed artistic director of the Sydney Dance Company in Australia. Tragically, just two months later in August 2007, she was killed in a car accident in Sydney. To honor her memory, her legacy was formalized through a charitable structure based in Germany. The foundation was officially registered in Stuttgart, Germany, as a tax-privileged charity under the name Tanja Liedtke Stiftung. To facilitate activities in Australia, the Tanja Liedtke Gift Fund was created in 2008 as a sub-fund of the Perpetual Foundation Gift Fund, mirroring the vision, aims, and priorities of the German entity.

OCCASIONS AND MEANING
The core purpose of the Tanja Liedtke Foundation is to support the enrichment and advancement of contemporary dance theatre and to develop artistic connections between Australia and Europe. The foundation fulfills this mandate by funding residencies, fellowships, and production awards. Its inaugural Tanja Liedtke Fellowship was offered in partnership with Radialsystem V – New Space for the Arts and the contemporary dance company Sasha Waltz & Guests in Berlin. The inaugural fellowship was awarded to Australian dancer and choreographer Antony Hamilton. In 2011, the fellowship was awarded to Polish dancer and choreographer Katarzyna Sitarz, supporting a creative residency at Arts House Melbourne in March 2011 and participation in the development of a new collaboration by Australian choreographer Lucy Guerin.

NOTABLE FIGURES
The foundation honors dancer and choreographer Tanja Liedtke, whose career reached international acclaim prior to her death in 2007. Recipient choreographers and artists associated with the foundation's fellowships and awards include Antony Hamilton, Katarzyna Sitarz, and Australian choreographer Lucy Guerin. The foundation has also partnered with major performing arts entities and spaces, including Radialsystem V, Sasha Waltz & Guests, Arts House Melbourne, and the International Choreographic Competition Hannover at Staatstheater Hannover, where it introduced a new production award in 2021.

sections.origins_and_history: The Tanja Liedtke Foundation was established in July 2008 in honor of dancer and choreographer Tanja Liedtke, who was killed in a car accident in Sydney, Australia, in August 2007, two months after starting as artistic director of the Sydney Dance Company. The foundation is registered as a tax-privileged organization in Stuttgart, Germany as Tanja Liedtke Stiftung. In 2008, the Tanja Liedtke Gift Fund was also established in Australia as a sub-fund of the Perpetual Foundation Gift Fund to reflect the foundation's primary vision and aims.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The foundation's purpose is to support the enrichment and advancement of contemporary dance theatre and to build artistic connections between Australia and Europe. It achieves this through fellowships, international artistic residencies, and competition awards. Fellowship recipients engage in creative residencies and collaborative developments, such as residencies at Radialsystem V in Berlin or Arts House Melbourne.
sections.notable_figures: Dancer and choreographer Tanja Liedtke is the central figure in whose memory the foundation was created. Fellowship recipients and creative collaborators include Australian dancer/choreographer Antony Hamilton, Polish dancer/choreographer Katarzyna Sitarz, and Australian choreographer Lucy Guerin. Partner organisations include Sasha Waltz & Guests, Radialsystem V, Arts House Melbourne, and Staatstheater Hannover.
